attempted_claim: Let X be a real Banach lattice with a 1-unconditional basis indexed by an uncountable set Gamma, and let Y be an infinite-dimensional complemented subspace of X not assumed to be a sublattice. Is it true that either (i) there is an uncountable pairwise-disjoint family in X whose closed span Z is complemented in X by the coordinate band projection and linearly isomorphic to a complemented subspace of Y, or (ii) Y is linearly isomorphic to a complemented subspace of the closed span of countably many basis vectors (hence of a separable 1-complemented sublattice of X)? Disjoint means exactly disjointly supported (not almost-disjoint); complemented means bounded linear projection (not assumed contractive or positive, except Z in X is band-complemented).
decisive_failure: The investigation attempted exactly three concrete routes: projection-matrix support extraction, model-space verification and lifting, and almost-disjoint perturbation to exact disjointness. Each was blocked by an explicit structural obstruction documented in target_exit.json. No complete proof, disproof, counterexample, or independently auditable emergent finding was produced, and no target-adjacent alternative assessed could pass full Audit on originality and value.
